questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar quantity as it has only magnitude, no direction. Velocity, force and displacement are vector quantities.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of frequency is Hertz (Hz), named after Heinrich Hertz. 1 Hz = 1 cycle per second.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: If the mass of an object is 10 kg and it is moving with a velocity of 5 m/s, what is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic Energy = ?mv? = ? ? 10 ? (5)? = 5 ? 25 = 125 J.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which law states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions?
questions.explanation: Pascal's Law states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mirror formula?
questions.explanation: The mirror formula is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f = focal length, v = image distance, u = object distance (with sign convention).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the escape velocity of the Earth?
questions.explanation: The escape velocity of Earth is approximately 11.2 km/s. It is the minimum speed needed to break free from Earth's gravitational pull.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure electric current?
questions.explanation: An ammeter is used to measure electric current in amperes. It is always connected in series.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The refractive index of diamond is approximately:
questions.explanation: The refractive index of diamond is about 2.42, which gives it its characteristic brilliance and sparkle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate with chemical formula NaHCO?.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is known as laughing gas?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N?O) is commonly known as laughing gas due to its euphoric effects when inhaled.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 M HCl solution?
questions.explanation: pH = -log[H?] = -log(10??) = 3. HCl is a strong acid so [H?] = 0.001 M.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which element is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is a key component of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron is a chemical change as it forms a new substance (iron oxide). The others are physical changes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the mass of 1 mole of carbon dioxide (CO?)?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO? = 12 + (2?16) = 12 + 32 = 44 g/mol.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is used in fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is used in fire extinguishers as it cuts off the oxygen supply and cools the fire.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which vitamin is produced in the human body by sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin upon exposure to UV rays from sunlight.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which organ is known as the "master gland" of the body?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is known as the master gland as it controls the function of most other endocrine glands.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the normal resting heart rate (beats per minute) for a healthy adult human?
questions.explanation: The normal resting heart rate for adults is typically between 60 to 72 beats per minute.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the scientific name of the Indian national animal?
questions.explanation: The Indian national animal is the Royal Bengal Tiger, scientifically known as Panthera tigris.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which disease is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of Vitamin C. Rickets is caused by Vitamin D deficiency.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: The process by which plants make their own food is called?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy to produce food.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood cells are responsible for immunity?
questions.explanation: White Blood Cells (WBCs) are part of the immune system and fight infections.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum controls balance, posture and coordination of voluntary movements.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the smallest unit of life?
questions.explanation: Cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O- blood group is the universal donor as it lacks A, B and Rh antigens, so it can be given to any blood group.

questions.explanation: A book is made up of chapters. Similarly, a tree is made up of branches.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a man, a woman said, "He is the only son of my mother's father." How is that man related to the woman?
questions.explanation: Mother's father = Maternal grandfather. His only son = Maternal uncle. So the man is the woman's maternal uncle (Mama).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A is the mother of B. C is the father of A. D is the brother of A. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: D is the brother of A, and A is the mother of B. So D is the maternal uncle of B.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Rahul walks 10 km towards North, then turns right and walks 5 km. He then turns right and walks 10 km. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 10 km North ? turns right (East) 5 km ? turns right (South) 10 km. Net displacement = 5 km West. So he is in West direction.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Ram starts from point A and walks 5 km East. He turns right and walks 12 km. He then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from point A?
questions.explanation: Starts 5 km East ? turns right (South) 12 km ? turns right (West) 5 km. Net displacement = 12 km South. So distance from A = 12 km.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row. B is sitting between C and D. A is sitting to the immediate left of B. E is at the extreme right end. Who is sitting at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: Arrangement: C - A - B - D - E. So C is at the extreme left end.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All pens are pencils. Some pencils are erasers. Conclusions: I. All pens are erasers. II. Some erasers are pens. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: All pens are pencils, and some pencils are erasers. The erasers may or may not include pens. Hence neither conclusion definitely follows.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All cats are animals. All dogs are animals. Conclusions: I. Some cats are dogs. II. Some animals are cats. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: All cats are animals implies some animals are cats (II follows). But cats and dogs are separate groups, so some cats are dogs does not follow.

questions.explanation: Students liking at least one = 60 + 50 ? 20 = 90. Neither = 100 ? 90 = 10.

options: Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: Both assumptions are implicit. The statement recommends the soap for glowing skin, implying it is effective (I) and that people desire glowing skin (II).

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded by Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, in 1885.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse (1848-1856) to annex Indian states without a male heir.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India (1947-1948). C. Rajagopalachari was the last.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and presides over its proceedings.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
questions.explanation: Article 32 grants the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and is regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The river known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal' is?
questions.explanation: The Damodar River is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal' because of the frequent and severe floods it used to cause in West Bengal.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which state is the largest producer of coffee in India?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is the largest producer of coffee in India, accounting for more than 70% of total production.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Silk City' of India is?
questions.explanation: Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu is known as the 'Silk City' of India for its famous silk sarees.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The highest mountain peak in India is?
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8586 m) is the highest peak in India. Mount Everest is in Nepal, K2 is in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: In India, the concept of 'Budget' is mentioned in which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 112 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) of the government.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The full form of GDP is?
questions.explanation: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product. It is the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Economics'?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the 'Father of Indian Economics' for his work on Indian poverty and economic drain theory.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The SI unit of electric current is?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric current is Ampere (A). Volt is for voltage, Ohm for resistance, and Watt for power.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The chemical formula of common salt is?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride with chemical formula NaCl.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which type of lens is used in a magnifying glass?
questions.explanation: A convex lens (converging lens) is used in a magnifying glass to produce a magnified image.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal recipient?
questions.explanation: AB+ blood group is the universal recipient as it has no antibodies against A, B or Rh antigens, so it can receive blood from any group.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is the author of the book 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.explanation: The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment in the 1940s.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who wrote the Indian national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana' was written by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali and adopted as the national anthem of India in 1950.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian athlete won the first individual gold medal for India in the Olympics?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won the first individual gold medal for India in the 2008 Beijing Olympics in 10m Air Rifle shooting.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian cricketer has the nickname 'Captain Cool'?
questions.explanation: M.S. Dhoni is known as 'Captain Cool' for his calm and composed demeanor on the cricket field.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The term 'Grand Slam' is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Grand Slam in tennis refers to winning all four major tournaments: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Konark Sun Temple' is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Konark Sun Temple is located in Odisha. It was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in the 13th century.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which day is celebrated as 'Constitution Day' in India?
questions.explanation: 26 November is celebrated as Constitution Day to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution in 1949.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: When is International Yoga Day celebrated?
questions.explanation: International Yoga Day is celebrated on 21 June every year. The first International Yoga Day was celebrated in 2015.
